statement: For real Dirichlet Q(s)=sum_(n<=T^delta) a(n)n^(−s), delta<1/2, the shifted zero sum in HLZ Theorem 5 equals J(alpha,beta,T)+I(alpha,beta,T)+I(beta,alpha,T)+O_A(T(log T)^(−A)) for every fixed A>0. J and I are the exact expressions in journal equations (5) and (24).
hypotheses: Unconditional published input; |alpha|,|beta|<=c/log T, fixed small c; common fixed divisor-log coefficient envelope and |a(mn)| bounded by a constant times |a(m)a(n)|; the bounded unit coefficient is treated separately. The real-coefficient specialization avoids hidden conjugation conventions. Theorem 5 is distinct from the smoothing Lemma 6/Theorem 4. Sharp continuous input is independently reconstructed.

statement: Under RH, fixed-dimensional cosine/sine normalized prime arrays on p ≤ (log Y)^D with covariance Σ_Y → Σ finite tend to N(0, Σ) if and only if max_p(‖a_p‖ + ‖b_p‖) → 0. Sufficiency is effective with computable fixed parameters and convergence moduli.
hypotheses: Exact symmetric strict tail probability weighted by |ζ′|²/(1/4 + γ²). The covariance uses v_p = (1 − 1/p)/2. The real coordinate is centered by p^(−1/2) and the imaginary coordinate by 0. Necessity uses unrestricted qualitative comparison and Cramér’s theorem. Singular covariance is allowed. Orthant effectivity requires positive limiting marginal variances.

statement: Under RH, disjoint centered unnormalized cosine bands (log Y)^(a_i) < p ≤ (log Y)^(b_i) have independent Gaussian limits of variance (1/2) log(b_i/a_i), for fixed positive separated exponent intervals.
hypotheses: Columns tend to zero as their primes tend to infinity. The variance need not diverge. Standardized cumulative cutoffs at (log Y)^D have limiting correlation 1.

statement: Under RH, set L = log Y, b = log L, H = log b, and X_Y(u) = √(2/H) Σ_{p ≤ exp(b^u)} [cos(γ log p)/√p − 1/p]. For fixed 0 ≤ u₀ < 1, X_Y converges to standard Brownian motion restricted to [u₀, 1] in D with the J₁ topology. An effective conditional bounded-Lipschitz onset exists for computable parameters.
hypotheses: The same exact two-sign strict derivative-weighted law applies. The proof uses uniform subset fourth moments bounded by C(Σ 1/p)², exact reciprocal-clock interpolation, an all-time modulus, and finite-dimensional comparison. Numerical onset and the unweighted zero law are outside this result.

statement: A monic integral q-reciprocal polynomial of degree d with nonzero roots and integer q ≥ 1 is pure of radius √q if and only if K_{ij} = q^min(i,j) t_{|i−j|} is positive semidefinite for 0 ≤ i,j < d, where t_n = Σ α^n and t₀ = d. Its inertia is (c + b, b, d − c − 2b), with c distinct circle roots and b off-circle reciprocal-conjugate pairs.
hypotheses: Multiplicities are positive, and real coefficients give conjugate closure. Repeated roots and reducibility are allowed. Exact Newton traces through d − 1 and rational pivoting give a polynomial-bit algorithm. The classical power-sum Toeplitz criterion is credited to Heinig–Rost.

statement: Unconditionally, the distinct-critical-line derivative series satisfies 0.61649875288731141829 < C₂ < 1.075561. The tail beyond 10,000 is less than 0.45906151 by global variation of Q₂Z/t with rational parameters and a complete infinite residual bound.
hypotheses: Uses the existing full 160-bit census of 10,142 positive zeros, independent replays, and the director’s 192-bit bound. RH is used only to identify the tapered-array limit. The quartic splice near 0.65339 remains observational.

statement: A real equivariant central spectral space satisfying Artin multiplicity axiom 2.12 is impossible at a Galois field with a quaternionic irreducible representation of odd central Artin order. Such Q₈ fields exist, excluding a universal arithmetic-curve theory with these properties.
hypotheses: The audit pins the complete arXiv:2204.02714v2 and compares the published version. Real complexification gives even quaternionic multiplicity. The entire monomial Hecke witness has negative root number. An isolated realization over ℚ and conjectural complex or quaternionic coefficient theories are outside the obstruction.

statement: On page 6 of arXiv:2209.12832v2, the term +iCt outside the integral requires C = −B − Σ m/[γ(1 + γ²)]. The displayed coefficient has the opposite sign. The exact S♯ example F = 1 + 2i·4^(−s) gives −8 log 2/17 for the printed C and +8 log 2/17 for the required C.
hypotheses: Source equations (1.1) and (2.5)–(2.6), signed atoms −γ, and truncation x/(1 + x²) are fixed. The change is a deterministic translation. The Gaussian and jump measures, screw kernel, and real-part criterion are unchanged. Journal wording is unverified.

statement: Under RH, every subpower cutoff P(Y) → ∞ with log P = o(log Y) gives all fixed Gaussian moments of standardized W_P. At P = Y^θ with 0 < θ < 1/2, weak Gaussian convergence holds, and moments through 2k converge when kθ < 1/2.
hypotheses: Uses natural cosine coefficients 1/√p, exact H_P and V_P centering and variance, and the symmetric strict tail. The bounded-coefficient aggregate polynomial theorem precedes main-term expansion. The proof uses near-power truncation and an upper-band L^p bound. The endpoint θ = 1/2 and all moments at fixed θ remain outside the result.

statement: Under RH, for 0 < a < b < 1/4, let Δ_j = b^j − a^j. The cosine band mean tends to log(b/a) − 4Δ₁ + 2Δ₃/3 and its variance tends to (1/2) log(b/a) − 4Δ₁² + 4Δ₁Δ₃ − 4Δ₃²/9. The sine mean is zero and its variance tends to (1/2) log(b/a) − (3/2)Δ₂². The mixed covariance is zero.
hypotheses: Fixed band Y^a < p ≤ Y^b, coefficients 1/√p, and the symmetric strict tail. Ratio and product kernels differ by 12x²y². The proof uses the exact diagonal and aggregate D² support with 2b < 1/2. Covariance test functions retain the finite-rank correction and positive lower bound.

statement: Under RH, for 0 < a < b < 1/6, the centered cosine band third moment tends to −8Δ₁³ + 24Δ₁²Δ₃ − 8Δ₁Δ₃² + 16Δ₃³/27 < 0. For [a,b] = [1/20, 1/10], the value is −818904257/864000000000. No centered Gaussian weak subsequence is possible.
hypotheses: Aggregate D³ support requires 3b < 1/2. The repeated-prime term (3/2)H times the mean cancels the corresponding second-moment diagonal. Uniform fourth moments from |Re D|⁴ ≤ |D²|² give uniform integrability of the cubes. The full limiting band law remains unproved.

statement: Globally derivative-square tilted rooted CUE has the same limiting cosine and sine means and covariance as the arithmetic band under RH, and the same centered cosine third moment for b < 1/6. Its projection is onto polynomials of degrees 0 through N with the rank-two span of constant and linear coefficient vectors removed.
hypotheses: Uses the HKO joint Haar matrix and root-label tilt, includes the selected root, and takes the negative Fourier band observable with weights 1/k. The correspondence is k/N ↔ log p/log Y. The random matrix statements are unconditional and the arithmetic comparison assumes RH. The match covers the band means, covariance, and cosine cubic. A full joint third-moment tensor and law transfer remain outside its scope.

statement: The sharp shifted continuous moment with a fixed polynomial has uniform error O_ε(T^ε[y√T + √y T^(3/4)]) for bounded coefficient families with y ≤ T^δ and fixed δ < 1/2. It holds for |α|, |β| ≤ c/log T with fixed small c, includes the weights 1 and log(t/(2π)), and treats the χ′/χ correction separately. It is unconditional.
hypotheses: The direct product approximate functional equation uses aggregated integer frequency gaps, a Mellin diagonal shift of −1/4, sharp endpoints, low heights, and holomorphic extension across coinciding shifts. The proof avoids applying Pratt–Robles smoothing outside its stated range.
